The present writ petition has been filed for issuance of direction upo respondents to initiate process of acquisition under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and to pay appropriate compensation to the petitioner for utilizing his raiyati land appertaining to Plot Nos.
1519, 1533 & 1534, Mouza- Narayangarh, Jamabandi No. 50, P.S-Maheshpur, District-Pakur,
measuring an area of 14 Katthaa 10 Dhurs, 4 Katthas 5 Dhurs & 15 Katthas 02 Dhurs respectively (total area 1 Bigha, 13 Katthas & 17 Dhrus) for construction of Maheshpur-Pakuria road.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has the raiyati right over the lands in question.
Earlier he happened to be an employee of the Government of Bihar.
When he came back to his native place i.e. Village/Mouza-Narayangarh after retirement, he found that the aforesaid lands had been utilized for construction of Maheshpur-Pakuria road.
The name of the petitioner's father-Late Lakhan Kisku is still being shown in Register-II with respect to the lands in question and the rent receipt for the same was also issued till 2015.

Under the said circumstance, the petitioner represented the respondent authorities seeking compensation for utilising the said lands for construction of Maheshpur-Pakuria road, however, the same was not responded which has compelled him to prefer the present writ petition.

sentences.text:
Mr. Amitesh Kr. Geasen, learned A.C to A.A.G-IA appearing on behalf of the respondents, submits that if the petitioner prefers a fresh representation on the present issue before the respondent No.5,
an appropriate order in accordance with law will be passed within a time frame.

4. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and keeping in view the nature of the prayer made in the present writ petition, without entering into the merit of the case, the petitioner is given liberty to prefer a fresh representation on the present issue before the respondent No.5.

On receipt of the said representation, the respondent No.5, after verifying the relevant records and on providing an opportunity of hearing to the petitioner (if so needed), shall take an appropriate informed decision in accordance with law within three weeks from the date of filing of the said representation.
5. The present writ petition is accordingly disposed of with the aforesaid liberty and direction.

Satish/- (RAJESH SHANKAR, J)
